A1.justification: Both 24-page PDFs describe the same GPLA research. Text extraction and visual inspection support comparison of the main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete Appendices A–C.

before.justification: v4 reports original value-system construction, factor analyses, safety prediction, alignment experiments, and supplementary empirical analyses in Appendix B and Appendix C.

after.justification: v6 retains these original empirical results, including the factor loadings and reliability estimates, benchmarking results, and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same perception parsing, value generation/filtering, GPV measurement, and PCA construction. The BaseAlign extension, target distillation, and PPO alignment procedure also remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same ValueBench, GPV, ValueLex, and BeaverTails sources, SALAD-Bench safety evaluation, LMSYS-Chat-1M coverage analysis, and preference-based alignment task. No dataset, domain, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Tables 2–3 retain Schwartz's high- and low-level systems. Table 4 retains both the original Schwartz-specific baseline and the Schwartz baseline using GPV. Appendix C retains the same ValueLex comparison.

E3.justification: The 33 models, 21 profiling prompts, 123 measurement prompts, CFA splitting/bootstrap procedure, safety-prediction protocol, and alignment settings are unchanged. Appendix B.1 still evaluates 512 conversations under the same selection procedure.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same lexicon-coverage analysis, PCA scree plot, circumplex analysis, cross-dataset consistency checks, Schwartz correlations, safety-contribution analysis, and ValueLex case studies. No analytical question or supporting evidence is added or removed.

E5.justification: Tables 1 and 13 retain the same Cronbach's alpha estimates and 95% confidence intervals; Table 3 retains the same ± reporting. There are no changes to disclosed runs, seeds, bootstrap practices, or significance testing.

E6.justification: Numerical and qualitative results match throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 3 retains 81±15, 74±16, and 87±9, while Table 4 retains the same harmlessness/helpfulness results, including -1.26/2.16 for the proposed system.

T1.justification: Equations 1–5 retain the same CFA model, Bradley–Terry formulation, target-distillation objective and minimization argument, and alignment objective. Mathematical typography changes do not alter definitions, assumptions, or reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: GPLA, a five-factor LLM value system, and three benchmarking tasks supporting claims of superior validity and utility relative to Schwartz's values.

C2.justification: The factor, circumplex, safety, and ValueLex interpretations remain unchanged. Both versions retain the limitations concerning English-only value measurement and the assumption of a single consistent alignment target.

D1.justification: Appendix A retains the model list, prompt template, dataset links, two 48-GB NVIDIA L20 GPUs, approximately 16,000 preference pairs, masking modification, and early-stopping details. The added funding acknowledgements do not revise technical or reproducibility information.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged, including the relationship to traditional psycho-lexical approaches, Schwartz's framework, GPV, BaseAlign, and ValueLex. Bibliography differences are formatting and pagination changes.

P1.justification: v6 adds an Acknowledgements section before References and replaces main-text 'Appendix' cross-references with section symbols. Other differences primarily concern spacing and typography; the scientific prose and section organization are retained.

P2.justification: Figures 2–3 are slightly resized and repositioned, and text and references reflow across pages and columns. The same figures, captions, tables, and table structures remain, without substantive display redesign.

improvement.justification: v6 adds funding acknowledgements and makes modest presentation adjustments, while preserving the scientific content, evidence, limitations, and reproducibility information. Readability remains broadly comparable; these edits establish no meaningful net improvement or deterioration in overall paper quality.
